data.title: Content Localised to Exploit a Regional Grievance
data.summary:
Campaign content is produced in local language and idiom and keyed to a grievance
specific to one site or region, indicating preparation rather than translation of a
generic message.
data.description:
Localisation is expensive, and its presence raises the assessed investment behind a
campaign. Producing content that reads as locally written — correct idiom, local
references, awareness of a dispute that was never national news — requires either local
operators or a sustained research effort.

It also makes the content far more effective. An audience that recognises its own
situation described accurately extends credibility to the rest of the message, including
the parts that are fabricated.

Localised campaigns tend to be invisible to central monitoring, which searches in the
headquarters language. Where one localised cluster is found, look for others before
concluding the campaign is confined to a single site.
data.recommendation:
* Monitor in the languages of every site, not only the head office language.
* Engage local management in the assessment; they can identify which grievances are real
  and which have been manufactured, and central staff usually cannot.
* Resolve or acknowledge the genuine local issue; a campaign built on a real grievance
  cannot be addressed by communications alone.
data.short_recommendation: Monitor in local languages and involve local management.
